title: Defining Advanced Allocation Records

children:
Advanced allocation records allow the allocation process to use percentages 
 when attempting to allocate quantity for a shipment line (this 
 process is sometimes called variable quantity or percent allocation). 
 The allocation process will only look in one location (or one license plate in one location) when performing advanced allocation. You will define these minimum/maximum percentages on the Advanced Allocation Window. It is also possible to manually indicate that a shipment line should use the advanced allocation process, whether an advanced allocation record exists for this item or not. You can indicate the minimum/maximum percentages that will be used for this line only.
The following is discussed in this topic:
Procedures: Creating an Advanced Allocation Record
Open the Advanced Allocation Window. Create a new record.

Select the Item 
 Class Button if you want to define an advanced allocation record 
 for an entire item class.

Select the Item Button if you want to define an advanced allocation 
 record for a specific item.

Use the Allocate 
 Full Location Quantity Checkbox to indicate if you want the system 
 to attempt to find a location where it can allocate the exact amount that 
 is required for the shipment line. If the system does not find this 
 location, allocation will fail.

Use the Allow 
 Percent Allocation Checkbox to indicate that you want the system 
 to use the advanced allocation process when attempting to allocate 
 quantity on a shipment line. To use this percentage allocation, you will need 
 to enter values for the minimum and maximum percentage fields (as described 
 below).

Use the Minimum 
 and Maximum Allocation Percentage Fields to indicate the thresholds that the system should use for performing variable quantity allocation. Note that these percentage fields refer to the line quantity, not the location's quantity. For example, suppose 
 you define an advanced allocation record for Item A (garden hose), and 
 indicated that you want to allow percent allocation. A customer then orders 100 feet of 
 garden hose:

- If the Minimum Percentage=100% 
 and the Maximum Percentage=110%, then the system would be able to allocate 
 a quantity of Item A in the range of 100 to 110 feet.

- If the Minimum Percentage=100% and the Maximum Percentage=100%, 
 then the system would have to allocate the exact quantity of Item A (100 
 feet).
NOTE: If both these percentages are set to 100%, then the system will need to find the exact detail quantity to allocate from a location, or allocation will fail.

Press OK. 
 The system will create your record.

If you create an advanced allocation record that has both the Allocate Full Location Quantity and the Allow Percent Allocation checkboxes not selected, the system will allocate this item/item class as if an advanced allocation record did not exist.
Suppose you have an item defined in the application that requires advanced allocation processing, such as a garden hose.
The item has the following advanced allocation settings:
Allocation Full Location Quantity Checkbox = not selected
1. You have a shipment line that requires 25 Feet of garden hose.
2. When the system attempts to allocate quantity for 25 Feet of an item, it finds that there is a location/license plate available with this item:
3. Therefore, allocation would succeed because a unique location/license plate does not currently exist that meets the minimum allocation percentage range (which in this case would be 23 Feet).
The item has the following advanced allocation settings:
Allocation Full Location Quantity Checkbox = selected
1. You have a shipment line that requires 25 Feet of garden hose.
2. When the system attempts to allocate quantity for 25 Feet of an item, it finds that there are only two location available in the warehouse with this item:
3. Therefore, allocation would fail because a unique location/license plate does not currently exist that meets the minimum allocation percentage range (which in this case would be 23 Feet).

        Example Scenarios...
        Suppose you have an item defined in the application that requires advanced allocation processing, such as a garden hose. 
         
        Scenario 1 - One Location Fulfills Allocation
        The item has the following advanced allocation settings:
        
            Allocation Full Location Quantity Checkbox = not selected
            Allow Percent Allocation Checkbox = selected
            Minimum Allocation Percentage = 95%
            Maximum Allocation Percentage = 110%
        
        1. You have a shipment line that requires 25 Feet of garden hose.
         
        2. When the system attempts to allocate quantity for 25 Feet of an item, it finds that there is a location/license plate available with this item:
        
            
                
                
                
                
                    
                        
                            Location
                        
                        
                            License Plate
                        
                        
                            Available Quantity
                        
                    
                    
                        
                            001-123-456
                        
                        
                            LP001
                        
                        
                            25 Feet
                        
                    
                
            
        
        3. Therefore, allocation would succeed because a unique location/license plate does not currently exist that meets the minimum allocation percentage range (which in this case would be 23 Feet). 
         
         
        Scenario 2
        The item has the following advanced allocation settings:
        
            Allocation Full Location Quantity Checkbox = selected
            Allow Percent Allocation Checkbox = selected
            Minimum Allocation Percentage = 95%
            Maximum Allocation Percentage = 110%
        
        1. You have a shipment line that requires 25 Feet of garden hose.
         
        2. When the system attempts to allocate quantity for 25 Feet of an item, it finds that there are only two location available in the warehouse with this item:
        
            
                
                
                
                
                    
                        
                            Location
                        
                        
                            License Plate
                        
                        
                            Available Quantity
                        
                    
                    
                        
                            001-123-456
                        
                        
                            LP002
                        
                        
                            15 Feet
                        
                    
                    
                        
                            001-123-456
                        
                        
                            LP003
                        
                        
                            10 Feet
                        
                    
                
            
        
         
        3. Therefore, allocation would fail because a unique location/license plate does not currently exist that meets the minimum allocation percentage range (which in this case would be 23 Feet).
